reason: The regular people and soldiers (עַם הָאָרֶץ, שָׂרֵי הַמֵּאוֹת, הָרָצִים) are consistently portrayed in a positive light throughout this narrative from 2 Kings 11. The commanders follow Jehoiada the priest's instructions faithfully and carefully ('וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֞וּ שָׂרֵ֣י המאיות הַמֵּא֗וֹת כְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּה֮'). Crucially, when the rightful king is restored, the people respond with joy and celebration: 'וְכָל־ עַ֤ם הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ שָׂמֵ֔חַ וְתֹקֵ֖עַ בַּחֲצֹֽצְר֑וֹת' (the people rejoiced and blew trumpets). At the narrative's conclusion, they experience peace and happiness: 'וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח כָּל־ עַם־ הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהָעִ֣יר שָׁקָ֑טָה' (all the people rejoiced and the city was peaceful). Their support for righteous authority and their positive emotional state present them favorably.
